observations: Photo 0: Blue cast-body gear reducer with a yellow output shaft/coupling visible; mounted on a base/foot with bolt holes.
Photo 1: Side view shows the reducer body and output shaft end; no nameplate/ratings visible.
Photo 2: Opposite side view shows the housing and mounting feet; no model/serial plate visible.

identity.kind: gear reducer (cast body) for industrial drive

claims.claim: Gear reducer 15 to 20hp cast bodies types
claims.evidence: No visible nameplate/spec label in photos 0-2 to confirm the 15–20hp rating or exact type.

risks.risk: Unknown gear ratio/output speed and shaft type (keyed/spline size), which strongly affects compatibility and value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the nameplate showing gear ratio, output speed (rpm), input speed (rpm), and shaft details (keyway/spline dimensions).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used gear reducer with unknown ratio and unknown compatibility (worst-case: may not match the required speed/shaft).

risks.risk: Unknown condition (backlash, bearing wear, oil leaks) because no inspection/operation evidence is shown.
risks.proof: Video clip of it running (or at least turning smoothly by hand with no grinding) plus close-ups of seals and any oil leakage points.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven to be in good working condition (worst-case: needs service/overhaul).

risks.risk: Unverified power rating (seller says 15–20hp) may be incorrect or for a different duty/input speed.
risks.proof: Nameplate photo showing rated horsepower (or kW), service factor/duty, and input speed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lower end of the claim only as a rough guide, but treated as unverified until confirmed by the plate.

risks.risk: Missing or incorrect mounting orientation/foot pattern and coupling interface.
risks.proof: Photo with a tape measure showing bolt-hole spacing on the base and a close-up of the output shaft end interface.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring adaptation if mounting/coupling doesn’t match.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the nameplate/label (ratings: hp/kW, input rpm, output rpm, gear ratio, model/serial).
Close-up of the output shaft end (keyway/spline size) with a ruler/tape measure.
Video of operation (or at minimum: smooth hand rotation) and close-ups of seals for oil leakage.
Bolt-hole spacing on the mounting feet (measurements) to confirm fit.
response.reason: The photos show a cast-body gear reducer, but the key pricing drivers (model/ratio, rated hp/kW, input/output speeds, and condition) are not readable/verified from the images. Without the nameplate and condition proof, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
